p01.label: Village of the Te’kula

evidence.quote: DM: Um. Okay. So we start as you're leaving the village of the Te'kula following Theba and your friends back into the material world from the village out of time, after having killed the great dragon, and spent some time, um, helping, ah, Theba and the Deno'qai, um, get back on their feet. And as you walk out of the forest you can feel the vibrations of this pocket dimension around you, shimmering faster and faster as the energy that holds the realm begins to unravel. And as you walk forward, the world fades around you, and you can feel the strands of the magic of this dimension stretching and breaking. And with a snap, you see your friends in a jumbled collection of images: a ship approaching a jagged coastline of an unfamiliar island, a dense tropical forest, a forest of pines and maples high on a mountain slope. And as Delwath, Wellby and Kenzo are pulled away from you, you hear Wellby's voice in your mind just for a moment: "Find your way to the Feywild, to the portal near Eudomes's Tower. We'll meet there again."

p01.note: The Neshet note identifies Te’kula village; its modern Material Plane position does not replace this departure from the village’s pocket dimension.

evidence.quote:
DM: Ah, they seem to be—so, there's a few things you do pick up from the book that may or may not be true, but seem to be consistent.

DM: So one is, um, the Feywild: the sun never moves. The sun doesn't move in time; the sun moves in space. So as you go— as you go west, it gets lighter and lighter, and as you go east it gets darker and darker—or no, yeah. And as you go—as you go west it gets lighter and lighter, and as you go east it gets darker and darker.

p03.label: Prince of Luck’s domain

evidence.quote: DM: Um, and she—she like—they all have now stopped laughing and—and look, ah, somewhat serious for a moment, says the one in front of you. She says: "That's— that's the Prince of Luck's domain. You must come to his court, should you wish to visit. Strangers may not wander."

p03.note: The Fortune’s Rest and session-61 notes identify the realm; that name is not spoken here.

evidence.quote: DM: You are— it's interesting—you are not—you are no longer on that plane, you know. You are in our world now.

p04.label: Arrival meadow

evidence.quote:
DM: In the next moment you find yourself on the ground in the middle of a large meadow. Around you, flowers are in bloom. There are petals slowly unfurling into butterfly wings as you watch. One flower takes off in a burst of tiny seeds flying into the air and fluttering around in a mesmerizing dance. But the flower stalk it just left wilts and melts, the tiny seeds knocked by its wings, settling and already beginning to sprout in the ground.

DM: In the—in the distance, away from the sun, maybe a few hundred feet, but distance again is hard to judge, you see the eaves of a forest. The trees shining in the afternoon light, the golds and reds of, and browns of oak and maple leaves, seeming to shimmer with an internal glow, always on the edge of dropping to the ground, but never quite doing so.

DM: In the direction of the sun, a meandering stream flows across the meadow. Although it's not wide, it seems to stretch, and you see the glint of marshy pools, and in places water that seems to flow with a mind of its own, seeping around the trunks of trees, forming pools and marshes full of cattails, moving slowly as if in the wind, although you feel no breeze. Beyond, mists rise from a small pond, and you can only dimly glimpse the far shore trees in the shadowy mists. So what would you like to do?

p04.note: Session 61 (DuFr) identifies the arrival realm as Fortune’s Rest. The transcript’s early domain warning is later clarified as referring to the mountain, so that warning alone does not establish the meadow’s containment.

p05.label: Crystal Mountain

evidence.quote: DM: And then you are hurtling towards the ground in the late afternoon light, images coming into focus as your fall begins to slow, a tangled forest studded with meadows below you, bursting with color. In the distance, far in the distance—although distance is hard to judge here, you're not sure whether it's, you know, five ten miles or hundreds of miles away. Um, a single mountain made of dazzling, multicolored crystal rising above misty low-lying clouds. You hear a waterfall but the river must be hidden in the vibrant reds and golds and greens of the leaves of the forest below. The sun sits low in the sky, late afternoon, bathing the landscape in a golden light, giving the place a timeless quality that you can't quite shake.

p05.note: Crystal Peak’s composition and the Prince’s storm commission resolve the mountain’s identity. The pixies claim it belongs to the Prince. The current Crystal Peak note places it between Fortune’s Rest and Shimmersong without settling that session-era boundary.
